thread:
sasha: Hey team — running into TLS errors in the JS SDK when users are behind our corp proxy. Error is `unable to verify the first certificate`. Works fine when I curl the endpoint with --insecure. Anyone seen this with the SDK and MITM proxies? :thinking:

devon: Yup, corporate proxies usually resign TLS with an internal CA. Node/OpenSSL will fail unless that CA is trusted. Which platform are you on? macOS? Linux?

sasha: macOS Ventura + homebrew Node 20. Also reproduces in our CI (ubuntu-22). The error stack points to `tls.connect` in the SDK streaming path. Not sure if it's the HTTP client or gRPC path.

liam: Quick checklist: 1) Is SSL_CERT_FILE or NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS set? 2) For Python the requests lib uses certifi; you may need to patch certifi with the corp CA or set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE. 3) For Node, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS works but note it replaces default CAs in some Node versions if you export it.

sasha: I tried `export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/path/to/corp.pem` and restart, still failing on streaming resume (KV cache connect) but regular REST calls succeed.

julia: Are streaming connections using a separate TLS stack (e.g., gRPC/native bindings)? If streaming goes over HTTP2 via a native layer, it may not read NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS. Which transport does the SDK use?

sasha: SDK debug shows `transport: http2` and the stack has `native-http2` bindings on mac. So sounds like a native OpenSSL layer.

liam: For native/OpenSSL you usually need the OS truststore updated (add corp CA to Keychain on macOS and to /etc/ssl/certs on Linux) or run the binary with SSL_CERT_FILE pointing at a bundle that includes system + corp CA. NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS sometimes only affects Node's JS TLS, not native modules.

devon: Another trick: run `openssl s_client -connect inference.redwood.ai:443 -showcerts` from inside the corp network and inspect the cert chain. If the proxy is resigning, you'll see the corp issuer in the chain.

sasha: I ran that; chain shows issuer "Internal Corp Proxy CA". So yes it's resigning. I added corp CA to System Keychain and now streaming connects locally. CI still fails.

liam: CI likely uses a minimal container image that doesn't include the system CA update. Two options: 1) bake the corp CA into CI images' /usr/local/share/ca-certificates and run update-ca-certificates, or 2) point the SDK to a bundle via env var at test runtime.

julia: For the Python SDK we added support for an env var REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE so users can pass a path to a cert bundle and both requests and our streaming native client pick it up. Maybe add same to Node SDK so users behind MITM can opt in?

sasha: Nice. Where is that env var documented? I couldn't find it.

liam: It's in an older PR for the python client only. We should standardize across SDKs: REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE or REDWOOD_TLS_CA. SDK owners: can we add consistent env handling? Node: check both NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS and REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE; Python: prefer REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE but fallback to REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE. Java: look at javax.net.ssl.trustStore.

julia: I'll file a tiny RFC and a devex doc. Proposed behavior: 1) If REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE set -> SDK uses that bundle for all transports (HTTP, HTTP2, native). 2) If not set -> fallback to platform default. 3) Add troubleshooting section with openssl and curl examples.

devon: Also doc the gotcha that on Node, providing NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS may not affect native http2 modules; recommend REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE for consistency.

sasha: Quick follow-up: we ran into mTLS requirement for a customer on Redwood Private. They asked for client cert auth from their side. Any pointers?

liam: For mTLS you need two things: 1) SDK supports loading client cert + key (PEM) and presenting it on TLS handshake; 2) Server must request client cert. We have a patch in eng-runtime to enable client certs in the dedicated routing layer. Node SDK currently accepts env vars REDWOOD_CLIENT_CERT and REDWOOD_CLIENT_KEY paths. Python has client_cert=(cert_path, key_path) param. Check the private deployment docs for exact TLS handshake expectations.

julia: Sasha, can you drop the CI container base image name? We can add a quick build step to inject corp CA for infra tests.

sasha: CI uses `ghcr.io/redwood/base:slim-2024-11`. I'll open a PR to add `/etc/ssl/certs/corp.crt` and run `update-ca-certificates` in the pipeline.

devon: Thanks. Two action items: 1) Julia - add REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE docs and troubleshooting snippet; 2) Liam - add Node SDK hook to respect REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE for native transports. Sasha - PR for CI image.

ci-bot: New issue created: RDWSDK-4123 "Standardize CA bundle env var across SDKs" (assigned to julia).

sasha: Awesome, thanks all. Leaving this thread so others can follow. If anyone hits a similar stacktrace (attach logs) I'll try to capture the openssl output from CI container. :thumbsup:
